claims.scope: CLOB post-only order admission via best-price check versus matching engine expiration handling

preconditions.text: An attacker places a small, soon-to-expire order at the top of the book.; After expiration, the order remains in the price tree.; A new post-only order is submitted at the same or better price than the expired order.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: 1. An attacker places a small, soon-to-expire order at the top of the book
2. After expiration, the order remains in the price tree but is skipped during matching
3. New post-only orders at the same or better price are rejected due to the expired order still being considered in the best price check

safety.text: A post-only order should be rejected as would-fill only when it would actually match against a non-expired existing order.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: 2. However, the matching engine (`_matchIncomingBid()`/`_matchIncomingAsk()`) correctly skips expired orders during actual matching
3. This creates a scenario where a post-only order is rejected due to an expired order that wouldn't actually match against it

effects.text: preventing legitimate trading strategies from functioning as intended
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

assumptions: The expired order is the best price returned by getBestAskPrice()/getBestBidPrice() at the time of the post-only check.
The matching engine would skip the expired order, so the new post-only order would not actually match against a non-expired order.
The post-only order is a legitimate trading strategy that should function as intended when it would not actually fill.
